input.quote: 10.5 Governing Law. This Agreement shall be governed and construed and enforced in accordance with the laws of the State of New York applicable to contracts made and to be performed exclusively in that State without giving effect to the principles of conflict of laws.
input.rationale: Section 10.5 selects New York law, which is our preferred governing law, and the document contains no arbitration or foreign venue provision (searches for "arbitration" and "jurisdiction" return nothing). However, the clause specifies no dispute forum, so it falls short of the preferred position requiring exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County. Minimal fix adds that venue sentence while leaving the governing law wording untouched.

ops.oldText: without giving effect to the principles of conflict of laws.
ops.newText: without giving effect to the principles of conflict of laws. Each Party irrevocably submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York with respect to any dispute arising out of or relating to this Agreement.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] New York law already matches our accepted position, so we only added an exclusive venue in the state and federal courts in New York County. The clause is otherwise silent on forum, which leaves disputes open to being pulled into an unfamiliar or foreign venue.
proposal.summary: Add exclusive New York County court venue to the New York governing law clause.
